title: data-labeling-cleanup-scratchpad-maya
content:
Scratchpad: data labeling cleanup + edgecase notes (personal)

Purpose:
- Quick personal notes while cleaning up label set for 'reply-intent' dataset.
- Capture recurring edge cases, sample annotations, and questions to discuss with Asha/Ryan before finalizing guidelines.

High-level problems observed:
1) Ambiguous system messages: some examples include assistant/system instructions concatenated with user text. Labelers sometimes mark those as 'no-intent' because they interpret as instructions rather than user intent. Need rule: drop system prompts before labeling OR treat message body only as labelable text.
2) Multi-intent utterances: e.g., "Can you set an alarm for 7 and tell me the weather?" -> Should be multi-label OR primary intent selection? Current dataset is single-label. Suggest: label primary intent as first actionable request (alarm), add "secondary-*" tag in metadata for multi.
3) Very short utterances like "Thanks" or "Cool" often labeled 'gratitude' or 'ack'. Decide canonical label set: gratitude OR acknowledgement -> map to 'acknowledgement' to reduce sparse classes.
4) Implicit intents: "I'm so tired" -> sentiment vs request for help. If no explicit ask, label as 'statement' not 'help_request'. Add note: only label as help_request if explicit ask or strong context (e.g., preceding turn asks for help).

Concrete labeling rules (draft):
- Preprocessing: strip system/assistant prefixes (anything starting with "System:" or "Assistant:") before labeling. If stripping changes meaning, flag for review.
- Single vs multi-intent: if utterance contains >1 distinct actionable intents, label primary by first verb-based request and add a "multi-intent" metadata tag. Do NOT invent secondary labels in main label field.
- Short acknowledgements: map to 'acknowledgement' (merge gratitude/ack/confirm into one class).
- Questions without clear intent (rhetorical) -> label 'statement'.
- URLs/emails/mentions: if the content is purely a URL or contact info, label 'contact-shared' or 'link-share'.

Edge case examples (annotate samples):
- "Can you remind me at 3? Also what's the traffic like?" -> label: remind-set; add tag: multi-intent.
- "System: do not reply
User: Please summarize this for me" -> strip system line, label: summarize.
- "Hey I can't sleep :-(" -> label: statement. If previous context shows they asked for tips -> help_request.
- "Thanks!" -> acknowledgement.
- "Open the pod bay doors, HAL" -> playful/command? label 'command' and tag 'sarcasm' if contains known fiction references (optional).

Quality cleanup checklist (to run on sample batch):
- [ ] Remove duplicated training examples (exact match after whitespace normalization).
- [ ] Normalize whitespace and lowercase for dedupe only (preserve original text in dataset field).
- [ ] Flag examples with label confidence < 0.6 (from annotator agreement).
- [ ] Audit top 100 most frequent 'statement' examples for label drift.
- [ ] Review 50 random examples where 'multi-intent' tag was added to ensure primary selection rule consistent.

Open questions / to discuss with leads:
- Do we want to support multi-label training later? If yes, we should stop collapsing secondary intents now. (ask @Asha)
- Triage severity: how strict should we be about stripping system messages? Risk: stripping can remove important context for intent. Proposal: strip by default, but keep raw text and add flag 'stripped_system=true' in metadata. (Note: metadata approach only for final schema, not part of current single-label CSV)
- Class consolidation: merge gratitude+ack? vote: +2 from my sampling but need product input for downstream metrics.

Notes for annotation UI updates:
- Add checkbox for 'multi-intent' when labeler sees >1 actionable request.
- Add dropdown reason when marking 'statement' to capture whether it's rhetorical, sentiment-only, or context-dependent.

Action items (next week):
- Sync with Asha & Ryan: go over 30 prototypical edge cases (scheduled Fri 10am)
- Implement preprocessing script draft (strip_system.py) and run on dev split -> produce report of changes (dup count, examples changed)
- Update labeling docs: create example gallery with golden examples for each rule (I will draft 20).

Quick search/refs I used while cleaning:
- Slack: #data-labeling thread (link in Confluence page)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-DB-789 (label taxonomy v0.3)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/labeling-prs/pull/78 (preprocessing prototype)

Random personal notes (messy):
- Consider adding rule to collapse "please" variants? Might help dedupe.
- Edge-case: nested quotes (user quoting assistant). If the quoted piece contains an instruction, treat only outermost user's current ask as labelable.
- Keep an eye on low-frequency labels (< 50 examples) — plan to merge/retire or create synthetic examples.

-- end scratchpad --

Todo: move this into a formal doc after Fri sync. "
